div.head: Chapter 18
div.p: And so that the full truth may be seen of the two kinds of tyranny we have set out and proved above — namely, the tyrannical entry and the tyrannical governance that the Spaniards have introduced in the Indies, by which they have destroyed them — we wish to bring here a proof that no one will be able to contest. And this is the preamble to a Royal Provision and general ordinance, to be observed throughout all the Indies, issued at Granada on the thirty-first of July of the year fifteen hundred and twenty-six. And it reads as follows:

Don Carlos, by the grace of God, etc. Forasmuch as we have been certified, and it is notorious, that through the disordered greed of some of our subjects who crossed to our islands and mainland of the ocean sea, by reason of the ill treatment they inflicted upon the native Indians of the said islands and mainland, both in the great and excessive labors they imposed upon them, keeping them in the mines to extract gold and in the pearl fisheries and in other works and enterprises, making them labor excessively and immoderately, not giving them the clothing and maintenance necessary for the sustenance of their lives, treating them with cruelty and lack of affection, much worse than if they had been slaves: all of which has been and was the cause of the death of a great number of the said Indians, and in such quantity that many of the islands and parts of the mainland were left barren and without any population of the said Indians and their native peoples; and that others fled and absented themselves from their own lands and places of origin, and went to the forests and to other places to save their lives and escape the said subjection and ill treatment: which was also a great impediment to the conversion of the said Indians to our holy Catholic faith, and to their not having come entirely and generally to a true knowledge of it; by which God, our Lord, is greatly disserved. And we are likewise informed that the captains and other persons who with our license and command went to discover and settle some of the said Indies and mainland, it being as it is our intent and desire to bring the said Indians to a true knowledge of God, our Lord, and of his holy faith, through the preaching of it and the example of learned persons and good religious, by doing them good works and treating them as neighbors, without their persons or goods receiving any force, compulsion, harm, or wrong; and this having been so ordered and commanded by us, with the said captains and our other officials and the people of such expeditions carrying specific instruction to that effect, moved by the said greed, forgetting the service of God, our Lord, and our own, they killed and had killed many of the said Indians in the discoveries and conquests, and took their goods from them, without the said Indians having given them just cause to do so, nor having first proceeded with or made the admonitions they were required to make, nor having offered the Christians any resistance or harm to the preaching of our holy faith: which, beyond being a great offense to God, our Lord, gave occasion and was to blame not only for the said Indians who received the said forces, injuries, and wrongs but many other neighboring peoples who had knowledge and intelligence of it rising up and gathering in arms against the Christians, our subjects, and killing many of them; and even the religious and ecclesiastical persons who never bore any fault, and suffered as martyrs preaching the Christian faith. For all of which we suspended and stayed the granting of licenses for the said conquests and discoveries, wishing to take steps and deliberate both concerning the punishment of what had passed and the remedy of what was to come, and to avoid the said harms and inconveniences, and to give order that the discoveries and settlements that hereafter were to be made should be carried out without offense to God, our Lord, and without the death or robbery of the said Indians, and without their being unlawfully made captives and slaves; so that the desire that we have had and have to extend our holy Catholic faith, and for the said Indians and unbelievers to come to knowledge of it, may be done without burden to our consciences, and we may pursue our purpose in the intention and work of the Catholic Monarchs, our lords and grandparents, in all those parts of the islands and mainland of the ocean sea that remain from our conquest yet to be discovered and settled. Which, having been considered with great deliberation by those of our Council of the Indies and consulted with us, it was agreed that we should order this letter in the said matter. For which reason we order and command that now and henceforth, both for the remedy of what has passed and in the discoveries and settlements that by our command and in our name are made in the said islands of the ocean sea, discovered and yet to be discovered within our limits and demarcations, there shall be observed and fulfilled what shall be contained below, in the following manner, etc.

And if by the year 1526 the devastations that the Provision describes had already been committed, let it be held as certain that from that time until the year sixty-three in which we now stand, they have been fifty times greater and many more in number and cruelty. This is evident because from that time forward there was laid waste and destroyed and robbed and depopulated New Spain, Guatemala, Yucatán, Nicaragua, and the great kingdoms of Peru, the new kingdom of Popayán, and the Río de la Plata, and Chile, and their surrounding lands and provinces.
